source_lines.98: - **No source fact is assumed.** GM Section 4, printed p. 27, reports all of (a) and the reversed-word equality as Garside's "elementary arguments" without reproducing the slides; here every move is reconstructed. The reversed-word equality $\rho(\Delta)=\Delta$ is proved in step 1.2 by the auxiliary recursion $U_{m-1}\Delta_{m-1}=\Delta_m$, the case $i\le m-2$ of (a) is derived in step 2.1 from the sliding lemma 1.1, the case $i=m-1$ is obtained in step 3.1 by transporting the case $i=1$ through the reversal anti-automorphism $\rho$, and the mirror identity, $\tau(\Delta)=\Delta$ and the centrality of $\Delta^2$ are proved in steps 4.1--5.2 from (a) and cancellation.
source_lines.99: - Note how the two triangular blocks are used: the *recursion* $\Delta_n=\Delta_{n-1}T_{n-1}$ couples a letter $\sigma_i$ with the index $n-i$, and the sliding lemma 1.1 realises exactly that shift inside a block. Reversal $\rho$ is not the same operation as $\tau$: $\rho$ fixes each letter but reverses products, $\tau$ permutes letters without reversing products.
source_lines.100: - Conventions: all identities are in the monoid $B_n^{+}$, so no inverse of $\Delta$ and no conjugation in a group are used; the phrase "conjugation by $\Delta$" in the title refers to the two-sided sliding $\sigma_i\Delta=\Delta\sigma_{n-i}$, which is a conjugation identity only after the Ore embedding of [[thm-the-ore-fraction-group-of-positive-braids-is-the-artin-braid-group]]. No choice principle is used.
